reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Fair: Look for bass to be hunting for bluegills and green sunfish along the rocks and edges of the weed beds early in the morning or late evening. They retreat out to deeper water during the day.

reports.title: Lake Geode fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Fair: Most bass have headed out to deeper water; expect to find them hunting the tree falls for bluegills and green sunfish on cloudy mornings.

reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Good: No Report: Marina areas and flooded pockets will hold bass feeding on minnows.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)

reports.text: Smallmouth Bass – Fair: Find smallmouth bass in slack water near rock and woody habitat; use spinnerbaits or soft plastics.

Bass – Good: There is a good population of largemouth bass.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Beeds Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Fair: Try drift fishing or troll tube jigs along the north shore.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Big Hollow Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Slow: Crappies remain in 6 feet of water in the flooded timber. Vertical jigging works best. Slip bobber and minnows are also picking up a few fish.
Largemouth Bass – Slow: Find bass around the drop-offs to deeper water; this steep sided lake has more than a few of those. Look for them down at about 6 feet, no deeper. Work the “shaded” bays and shores first.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Black Hawk Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie - Fair: Try fishing over the rock piles and from boat in 2-6 feet of water. Anglers have also had success in the fish house in Town Bay.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Try a plastic or crankbait near shallow rock piles and outcroppings.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Brushy Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Fish have moved to deeper habitat. Look for suspended fish near isolated brush and rock piles in 5-15 feet of water.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Use a plastic or crankbait in 6-10 feet of water or isolated vegetation and structure along the edge of the channel.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Casey Lake (aka Hickory Hills Lake) fishing report
reports.text:
Anglers are having success with bluegill, black crappie, largemouth bass, and channel catfish.
Black Crappie – Good: Find structure using electronics and jig colored tube jigs at various depths to locate fish; the south corner of the damn has been really good for crappie.
Largemouth Bass – Good: Anglers are catching bass on most everything thrown at them; try spinners, crankbaits, and topwater baits.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)

reports.text:
Black Crappie – Slow.
Largemouth Bass – Fair.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: George Wyth Lake fishing report
reports.text: Anglers have been fishing George Wyth Lake for largemouth bass.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Iowa Lake (Iowa Co.) fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Use minnows fished 4-8 down over deeper water. Some sorting is required; 8-inch and 10-inch fish are being caught.
Largemouth Bass – Good: Try fishing around remaining weeds or laydowns. Most fish are 1-2 pounds.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Belva Deer fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie - Slow: A few anglers early in the morning are still picking up a few in about 6 to 7 feet along the trees out from the beach. They are moving a little shallower as the summer wears on and the deeper water runs out of oxygen.
Largemouth Bass – Slow: Bass are trying to stay cool; look for them in about 6-7 feet of water out in the trees. Try soft plastic or weedless jigs early in the morning.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Darling fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Slow: Bass are hunting up in the rock piles in 6-8 feet of water early in the mornings.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Geode fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie - Slow: Crappies are out in deeper water for the summer. Try slow trolling in 8 to 10 feet of water along the drop-offs.
Largemouth Bass – Slow: Bass are out at the drop-offs; they have slid down the slope a little to cooler water to avoid the heat. They have decent oxygen at about 8-9 feet of water. Best bite is early or just as the sun goes down.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Macbride fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Fair: Try fishing shallow to mid-depth structure.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Sugema fishing report
reports.text:

Largemouth Bass – Good: Use spinnerbaits or jigs along rip-rapped shorelines and around the rock jetties. Try topwater lures early and late in the day.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lost Grove Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Slow: Crappies are out along the edge of the flooded timber in 8 to 10 feet of water. Try vertical jigging or slow trolling until you find them.
Largemouth Bass – Slow: Try vertically jigging in or along the outer edge of the flooded timber in 10-12 feet of water. Weedless rigged soft plastics can help you keep get out of the snags.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lost Island Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Fair.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 12 fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth Bass – Excellent: Bass are on the feed. Try plastic baits along shoreline weed beds during low water. Hit shady spots when the sun is bright.
Smallmouth Bass – Excellent: Cast inline spinners or crankbaits just off rock points to catch smallmouth feeding in the rocks. Lots of smallmouth have moved on to the wing-dams.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 13 fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth Bass – Excellent: Lots of bass are biting in the marina areas and backwater lakes. Some fish are moving out onto the vegetation lines; use plastic baits.
Smallmouth Bass – Excellent: Cast inline spinners just off rock points to catch smallmouth feeding on minnows. Many smallmouth are also on the wing-dams, especially in this low water.

reports.text:

Largemouth Bass – Good: Try fishing the edge of weed beds in backwater and side channel areas.
Smallmouth Bass – Good: Cast a spinner or crankbaits in current along the rocky shorelines.

reports.text:

Largemouth Bass – Fair: Bass are working back in the trees during the early morning. Try casting back in there with topwater baits and have some fun. You can hear them splashing around just after the sun gets up.

reports.text:

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Volga Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Good: Troll the deeper open areas of the lake. Crappies are out deep.
Largemouth Bass – Good: Use a crank or spinnerbait. Area interior rivers and streams are low. Recent rainfall didn’t bump rivers up much. Clarity is good on most area rivers and streams. Temperatures in the upper 80s during the day to 60s overnight. Possibility of scattered thunderstorms on Saturday. For current fishing information, please call the Chuck Gipp Decorah Fish Hatchery at 563-382-8324.

reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 12 fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth Bass – Excellent: Bass are on the feed. Try plastic baits along shoreline weed beds during low water. Hit shady spots when the sun is bright.
Smallmouth Bass – Excellent: Cast inline spinners or crankbaits just off rock points to catch smallmouth feeding in the rocks.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 13 fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth Bass – Excellent: Lots of bass are biting in the marina areas and backwater lakes. Some fish are moving out onto the vegetation lines; use plastic baits.
Smallmouth Bass – Excellent: Cast inline spinners just off rock points to catch smallmouth feeding on minnows.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 15 fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth Bass – Good: Try throwing spinners along the rock lines in Pool 15. Lots of rock is available; need somewhat strong current to hold smallmouth bass.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 9 fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Use artificial jigs or a crappie minnow along the fallen trees in 6-8 feet of water.
Largemouth Bass – Good: Try fishing the edge of weed beds in backwater and side channel areas.
Smallmouth Bass – Good: Cast a spinner or crankbaits in current along the rocky shorelines.

reports.title: Swan Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Fair.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Upper Iowa River (above Decorah) fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth Bass – Fair: Try fishing near undercut banks and current breaks. A flashy jig works well. Fly anglers using streamers are picking up some action.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Volga Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Good: Troll the deeper open areas of the lake. Crappies are out deep.
Largemouth Bass – Good: Use a crank or spinnerbait. Area interior rivers and streams are low. Clarity is good to excellent on most area rivers and streams. Temperatures in the upper 70s during the day to 50s overnight. Possibility of spotty showers through the weekend. For current fishing information, please call the Chuck Gipp Decorah Fish Hatchery at 563-382-8324.
